card.name: Linking words before a verb in formal prose
card.fires_on: Small linking or helper words (but, which, cannot, must, can, to) inside long formal, often older-style sentences. They sit right before the main verb, often one about limits or necessity.

modes.label: Conjunction or relative word
modes.description: A word like but or which joins a clause and leads into an abstract statement.

modes.label: Modal verb before a negation or claim
modes.description: Words like cannot, must or can appear in philosophical or legal statements, often just before a verb such as be defined or be adopted.
modes.example: Its boundaries<< cannot>> be defined with certainty.
